subject.title: Externally-registered cron jobs auto-enable without user confirmation, inherit expensive default model, no usage circuit breaker

question: Should externally or plugin-registered recurring cron jobs become disabled/confirmation-gated by default, or should OpenClaw preserve enabled-by-default compatibility while adding explicit warnings, model defaults, and circuit breakers?
rationale: Source inspection proves the gap, but choosing the permanent cron enablement, inherited-model, provider-spend, and plugin scheduling contract is a product/security compatibility decision.

options.title: Adopt provenance-gated consent
options.body: External, agent, and plugin recurring jobs would require explicit operator activation or a doctor/update diff before becoming enabled, with migration handling for existing jobs.

options.title: Preserve enabled default with hard guardrails
options.body: Keep existing jobs active by default but require explicit low-cost model/default selection, inherited-model warnings, and billing/auth circuit breakers before background polling runs.

options.title: Split immediate warnings from scheduler redesign
options.body: Add doctor/update visibility and model-risk warnings now while leaving the non-forgeable scheduling API and budget enforcement to the related RFCs.

recommendation.title: Adopt provenance-gated consent
recommendation.body: External, agent, and plugin recurring jobs would require explicit operator activation or a doctor/update diff before becoming enabled, with migration handling for existing jobs.

likelyOwner.reason: The current central implementation lines all blame to this recent area commit, and the decision spans cron, plugin scheduling, and model-selection behavior.
